SUPERSEDED_BY.note: All fields ABOVE this key are PRE-FIX (measured against the asymmetric round-half-up quantisation kernel that Plan 06-06 itself found and flagged in its own 'Deviations from Plan' -- 'a prediction sitting EXACTLY half a tick above the ask rounds UP and triggers a long; a prediction exactly half a tick below the bid also rounds UP and therefore does NOT trigger a short'). Plan 06-07 Task 0 (2026-09-24) fixed sim/kernel.py + sim/reference.py to a SYMMETRIC floor(long)/ceil(short) quantisation rule and re-measured. Kept here for audit trail, not deleted -- see this block for the corrected, canonical numbers.
SUPERSEDED_BY.MYSTERY_RESOLVED: 06-06's 'unexplained' divergence from 06-RESEARCH.md's baseline (2,192 trades / 294,554 ticks) is NOW EXPLAINED, not merely moot: the post-fix trades/closed_pnl_ticks above are an EXACT match to 06-RESEARCH.md's baseline. 06-06 ruled out 4 alternative candidate tie-break rules (06-RESEARCH.md Q2's own list) because every one of them applied ONE rounding rule uniformly to BOTH the long and short comparisons -- none of the 4 candidates tested was 'a DIFFERENT rounding rule per direction', which is the actual fix. The research prototype's own tie-break (whatever it was) evidently already matched the correct symmetric behaviour; the buggy kernel's shared round-half-up value did not.

trade_log_side_counts_POST_FIX.note: This kernel is flip-only, so trade-log side counts ALWAYS alternate 1:1 regardless of the quantisation rule -- this pair proves NOTHING about the bias and is recorded only because it was asked for. The actual before/after bias evidence is 'vectorised_trigger_row_counts_over_all_surviving_rows_PRE_VS_POST_FIX' below.

vectorised_trigger_row_counts_over_all_s.note: Counted over ALL 6,864,853 surviving decision rows (not just fills) -- whether that row's pred WOULD trigger long/short under each rule, independent of the flip-only state machine. This is what actually shows the bias and its removal.
vectorised_trigger_row_counts_over_all_s.interpretation: short_trigger_rows is IDENTICAL before and after (1,897,533 both) -- expected, because 99.96% of perfect-foresight pred values sit exactly on a half-tick boundary, and on an exact tie ceil(pred) (the new short-side rule) equals round-half-up(pred) (the old shared rule) by construction; only the long side's rounding direction changed (floor vs round-half-up-which-rounds-ties-up). long_trigger_rows dropped by 56,043 rows (2.91%) after the fix, removing the long-favoring bias the old shared rule introduced. The fixed rule is NOT guaranteed to produce exactly-equal long/short trigger counts (that would require the underlying market data's up-move vs down-move crossings to be exactly symmetric, which is a data property, not a rule property) -- post-fix, short now exceeds long by 1.51%, roughly the mirror image of the old 1.44% long excess, consistent with removing a directional mechanism bias rather than perfectly balancing the data.
